bpmProshop2026Review.title: Burton Custom Camber 2026 Snowboard Testbericht
bpmProshop2026Review.testSetupDisclosure: The reviewer says the team had ridden the Custom before and tried the new 2026 version, but does not disclose sample size, rider count, board length, exact snow conditions, or number of test days.
bpmProshop2026Review.observations: Describes strong edge hold on hard/icy pistes, high-speed composure, direct/agile edge changes, useful pop for jumps, and switch/all-mountain versatility; identifies deep-snow float and beginner accessibility as limitations.
bpmProshop2026Review.scoreUse: Same-season directional evidence, but insufficiently detailed to quantify individual score changes. Its high-speed stability claim conflicts with the chatter/high-speed ceiling noted by Board of the World and Snowboarding Profiles' 2025 sample; retain the existing stability estimate and document the disagreement rather than averaging review language into a numeric score. No external numeric score is mapped.

boardOfTheWorld.sampleScope: The main review tests the 2027 model; the reviewer separately rode the 2025/26 Custom at Big Snow indoor resort and reports similar ride character. The target-season exposure is limited and does not establish a full-season, multi-rider test.
boardOfTheWorld.observations: Supports carving and stability at ordinary resort speeds, but reports nose/tail chatter in chop and performance limits at very high speed. The review's light-powder exposure was limited; Custom is not presented as a deep-powder specialist. It also reports useful pop/jump and all-mountain versatility.
boardOfTheWorld.scoreUse: Directional evidence only. No external score is mapped numerically to the site's six editorial dimensions.

snowboardingProfilesHistorical.disclosedTest: 2025 model, 156 cm sample, tested 2024-02-06; hard artificial snow with icy sections and no new snow.
snowboardingProfilesHistorical.observations: Historical directional corroboration: carving and normal resort-speed stability are good, but the reviewer notes a high-speed ceiling, some chatter in crud, limited deep-powder suitability, and a need for sound technique. Its measured weight belongs to the 2025 156 cm sample and is not transferred to this 2026 158 cm seed.
snowboardingProfilesHistorical.scoreUse: Historical model-year proxy only; external sub-scores are not converted to the site's six dimensions.

editorialDecision.rationale: Stability is reduced modestly from 9 to 8.5 because Board of the World and Snowboarding Profiles' 2025 sample report chatter/high-speed limits, while the 2025-09-23 BPM Proshop report on the stated 2026 version claims strong high-speed composure but omits board length, conditions, test duration, and rider count. This unresolved evidence conflict supports retaining a cautious estimate rather than raising or lowering it further. The adjustment is editorial, not a conversion of another publisher's scale. Other dimensions remain unchanged because evidence is season-limited or insufficiently detailed; all six remain low-to-medium confidence, with value low due to missing local price provenance.
editorialDecision.copyDecision: Removed unsupported absolutes about near-zero high-speed chatter, effortless/crippling low-speed behavior, and rider mass threshold. Updated product construction terms to W26 manufacturer nomenclature.
